```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rathi_2021_belantamab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rathi_2021_belantamab"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12660>
* Supplement (Tables S1-S4 and the NONMEM control streams of all three
  models in the Supplementary Methods): available from the article page.

Rathi 2021 fitted three models sequentially. The ADC model was fitted first.
The total-antibody and cys-mcMMAF models were then fitted with the ADC
individual post hoc parameters as fixed inputs. Neither later model can be used
without the ADC model, so the three are packaged as one model with three
outputs:

| Output | Analyte | Units | Sub-model |
|--------|---------|-------|-----------|
| `Cc` | belantamab mafodotin ADC | ug/mL | Table 1 |
| `Cc_tab` | total antibody (ADC + naked antibody) | nM | Table S3 |
| `Cc_mcmmaf` | cys-mcMMAF payload | nM | Table S4 |

The dose (mg of ADC) goes into `central`. In the control streams 1 nM of ADC
is 152.1 ng/mL and 1 nM of cys-mcMMAF is 1.045 ng/mL; the model applies the
same factors.

# Population

Rathi 2021 pooled 291 patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma from
DREAMM-1 (phase I, n = 73, 0.03-4.6 mg/kg as a 1-h infusion every 3 weeks) and
DREAMM-2 (phase II, n = 218, 2.5 or 3.4 mg/kg as a 30-min infusion every
3 weeks; 24 of the 3.4 mg/kg patients received the lyophilised presentation).
The median age was 65 (34-89) years and the median body weight 74.0
(42.4-130) kg. 54% were men and 83% White. Median baseline albumin was 39.0
g/L, sBCMA 80.0 ng/mL and IgG 8.50 g/L (Table S2). The typical patient used for
the paper's exposure calculations is a 65-year-old man from DREAMM-2 weighing
75 kg, with sBCMA 100 ng/mL, IgG 10 g/L and albumin 40 g/L, receiving 2.5 mg/kg.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Rathi_2021_belantamab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Table 1 prints the ADC estimates to two decimals. The unrounded final
estimates appear as the fixed `$THETA` values in the total-mAb and cys-mcMMAF
control streams (Supplementary Methods), and those are the values used. Each
rounds to its Table 1 value.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| ADC two-compartment ODE, dose into central | n/a | Supplementary Methods ADC control stream (`ADVAN3 TRANS4`) |
| `lcl` (CL0) | log(0.936) L/day | Table 1 TVCL 0.94; control stream THETA(1) |
| `lvc` (V1, female) | log(4.47) L | Table 1 TVV1; THETA(2) |
| `lq` | log(0.781) L/day | Table 1 TVQ 0.78; THETA(3) |
| `lvp` | log(5.96) L | Table 1 TVV2; THETA(4) |
| time-varying CL `exp(IMAX t^GAMMA / (TI50^GAMMA + t^GAMMA))` | n/a | Results equation; control stream `CLT` |
| `cl_time_max` (IMAX, additive eta) | -0.327 | Table 1 -0.33; THETA(5) |
| `lcl_t50` (TI50) | log(53.9) day | Table 1; THETA(6) |
| `lcl_time_hill` (GAMMA) | log(4.30) | Table 1; THETA(7) |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.507, 0.500 | Table 1; THETA(17), THETA(10) |
| `e_alb_cl`, `e_alb_vc` | -0.972, -0.471 | Table 1; THETA(12), THETA(13) |
| `e_sexm_vc` | 1.14 | Table 1; THETA(14), applied as `THETA**SEX` with SEX = 1 for males |
| `e_sbcma_cl`, `e_igg_cl` | 0.126, 0.127 | Table 1; THETA(15), THETA(16) |
| `e_dose_low_vp`, `e_dose_low_cl` | 0.129, 0.623 | Table 1; THETA(20), THETA(21) |
| `e_study_dreamm1_vc`, `e_study_dreamm1_cl` | 0.66, 0.608 | Table 1; THETA(22), THETA(23) |
| ADC IIV (CL, V1, Q, V2, IMAX, TI50) | 35.0, 14.6, 37.8, 46.8, 123, 30.1 percent CV | Table 1 |
| `expSd` | sqrt(0.019) | Table 1 'additive SIGMA on log scale' |
| naked antibody ODE: ADC loses CL/V1, kdec of it to naked antibody, which is eliminated at CL/V1 - kdec | n/a | Supplementary Methods total-mAb `$DES` |
| `lkdec`, `e_dose_low_kdec` | log(0.0590) /day, 0.0001 (held constant) | Table S3 |
| total antibody = (ADC + naked) x CORR | n/a | Table S3 residual-error equation; Results |
| `lcal_slope_tab` (CORR) | log(1.14) | Table S3 |
| `e_study_dreamm1_cal_slope_tab`, `e_dose_low_cal_slope_tab` | 0.848, 0.846 | Table S3 |
| total-antibody IIV (Kdec, CORR) | 38.8, 7.58 percent CV | Table S3 |
| `expSd_tab` | sqrt(0.0516) | Table S3 |
| cys-mcMMAF input `(CL/V1) x A_ADC x DAR(t)` | n/a | Supplementary Methods cys-mcMMAF `$DES` |
| `DAR(t) = DAR0 exp(-RATE x TAD)`, reset at each dose | n/a | Results equation; control stream `DARF` |
| `lkdar` (RATE-DAR) | log(0.067) /day | Table S4 |
| `mdar` (DAR0) | 3.93 (held constant) | back-solved from the Results cys-mcMMAF Cavg (see Assumptions) |
| `lcl_mcmmaf`, `lvc_mcmmaf` | log(648) L/day, log(30.4) L | Table S4 |
| `lk12_mcmmaf` (K34), `lk21_mcmmaf` (K43) | log(74.9), log(5.62) /day | Table S4 |
| `e_sbcma_vc_mcmmaf`, `e_igg_vc_mcmmaf` | 0.131, 0.154 | Table S4 |
| `e_study_dreamm1_vc_mcmmaf` | 0.507, as (1 + theta) | Table S4; control stream `VSTUDY` |
| cys-mcMMAF IIV block (CL, V3, K43) | 0.100; 0.112, 0.260; 0, 0.257, 0.956 | Table S4 |
| cys-mcMMAF IOV (CL, V3), OCC 1, 2, 3, > 3 | 0.100, 0.185 | Table S4; control stream `IOV`, `IOV2` |
| DREAMM-1 VALA recalibration `1.486 x C - 8.360 pg/mL` | `cal_slope_vala` 1.486, `cal_int_vala` -0.008 nM | Methods equation; control stream `SLP`, `INT` |
| cys-mcMMAF residual error, DREAMM-2 | prop sqrt(0.051), add sqrt(0.0002) nM | Table S4 |
| cys-mcMMAF residual error, DREAMM-1 | prop sqrt(0.0851), add sqrt(0.0009) nM | Table S4 |

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Rathi_2021_belantamab")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

# Typical-patient exposures

Rathi 2021 (Results, 'Typical patient and impact of covariates on exposure
measures') reports the cycle-1 exposures of the typical DREAMM-2 patient after
2.5 mg/kg: ADC Cmax 36.5, Cavg 7.76 and Ctau 2.22 ug/mL, and cys-mcMMAF Cmax
917 and Cavg 217 pg/mL. The values are stated to be 1.36-fold higher at
3.4 mg/kg. Below, the typical patient is simulated without random effects and
the exposures are computed with PKNCA over the 21-day cycle.

```{r typical-events}
typ_cov <- data.frame(
  WT = 75, ALB = 40, SBCMA = 100, IGG = 10, SEXF = 0,
  STUDY_DREAMM1 = 0, DOSE_LOW = 0, OCC = 1
)
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.005), seq(1, 21, by = 0.05))))

make_typical <- function(id, dose_mgkg, cov = typ_cov, inf_h = 0.5) {
  amt <- dose_mgkg * cov$WT
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = 0, amt = amt, rate = amt / (inf_h / 24),
    evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_grid, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
    evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg")) |>
    cbind(cov[rep(1, nrow(dose) + nrow(obs)), , drop = FALSE])
}

typ_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_typical(1L, 2.5),
  make_typical(2L, 3.4)
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, typ_events,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
  keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r typical-nca}
nca_one <- function(sim, conc_col) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    dplyr::transmute(id, time, treatment, Cc = .data[[conc_col]]) |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
  dose <- typ_events |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 21, cmax = TRUE, cav = TRUE, clast.obs = TRUE)
  ))
  res
}

nca_adc <- nca_one(typ, "Cc")
# cys-mcMMAF reported in pg/mL: nM x 1045
typ$Cc_mcmmaf_pgml <- typ$Cc_mcmmaf * 1045
nca_mmaf <- nca_one(typ, "Cc_mcmmaf_pgml")

pub_adc <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~cav, ~clast.obs,
  "2.5 mg/kg", 36.5, 7.76, 2.22,
  "3.4 mg/kg", 36.5 * 1.36, 7.76 * 1.36, 2.22 * 1.36
)
pub_mmaf <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~cav,
  "2.5 mg/kg", 917, 217,
  "3.4 mg/kg", 917 * 1.36, 217 * 1.36
)

cmp_adc <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_adc, reference = pub_adc, by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", cav = "ug/mL", clast.obs = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_adc, caption = "ADC cycle-1 exposures of the typical DREAMM-2 patient: simulated vs. Rathi 2021 Results (3.4 mg/kg reference = 1.36 x the 2.5 mg/kg value, as stated in the paper). Ctau is the concentration at day 21. * differs from reference by >20%.")

cmp_mmaf <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_mmaf, reference = pub_mmaf, by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "cav"),
  units = c(cmax = "pg/mL", cav = "pg/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_mmaf, caption = "cys-mcMMAF cycle-1 exposures of the typical DREAMM-2 patient: simulated vs. Rathi 2021 Results. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

```{r typical-gate}
nca_val <- function(res, code, trt) {
  d <- as.data.frame(res)
  d$PPORRES[d$PPTESTCD == code & d$treatment == trt]
}
pct <- function(sim, ref) 100 * (sim - ref) / ref
# The typical patient is deterministic, so these gates are tight. The ADC model
# is transcribed directly; a mis-typed CL, V1 or covariate centre moves these
# by far more than 2%.
stopifnot(
  abs(pct(nca_val(nca_adc, "cmax", "2.5 mg/kg"), 36.5)) < 2,
  abs(pct(nca_val(nca_adc, "cav", "2.5 mg/kg"), 7.76)) < 2,
  abs(pct(nca_val(nca_adc, "clast.obs", "2.5 mg/kg"), 2.22)) < 2,
  # cys-mcMMAF Cavg is the quantity DAR0 was back-solved from.
  abs(pct(nca_val(nca_mmaf, "cav", "2.5 mg/kg"), 217)) < 2,
  # cys-mcMMAF Cmax is ~9% below the printed 917 pg/mL; see Assumptions.
  abs(pct(nca_val(nca_mmaf, "cmax", "2.5 mg/kg"), 917)) < 15,
  # Linear in dose above 1 mg/kg.
  abs(nca_val(nca_adc, "cmax", "3.4 mg/kg") / nca_val(nca_adc, "cmax", "2.5 mg/kg") - 1.36) < 0.001
)
```

## Half-life and time-varying clearance (Figure 3)

The Results state an initial typical ADC CL of 0.94 L/day with a half-life of
11.5 days, falling by 28% over time to give a half-life of 14.3 days. The
terminal half-life follows from the two-compartment micro-constants at t = 0
and at t much greater than TI50. The printed half-lives are reproduced with
the typical values themselves, i.e. with V1 = 4.47 L, which is the female
reference (the male factor of 1.14 is not applied). For the typical man the
half-lives are about 0.3-0.5 days longer.

```{r half-life}
p <- ui$theta
q <- exp(p[["lq"]])
vp <- exp(p[["lvp"]])
beta_hl <- function(cl, vc) {
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  log(2) / beta
}
cl0 <- exp(p[["lcl"]])
cl_inf <- cl0 * exp(p[["cl_time_max"]])
vc_ref <- exp(p[["lvc"]])
vc_male <- vc_ref * p[["e_sexm_vc"]]
hl <- rbind(
  `typical values (V1 = 4.47 L)` = c(initial = beta_hl(cl0, vc_ref), late = beta_hl(cl_inf, vc_ref)),
  `typical man (V1 x 1.14)` = c(initial = beta_hl(cl0, vc_male), late = beta_hl(cl_inf, vc_male))
)
knitr::kable(hl, digits = 2, caption = "ADC terminal half-life (day) at the start of treatment and after the full time-varying CL change. Rathi 2021: 11.5 and 14.3 days.")
round(100 * (1 - exp(p[["cl_time_max"]])), 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(hl[1, "initial"] - 11.5) < 0.1,
  abs(hl[1, "late"] - 14.3) < 0.1,
  abs(100 * (1 - exp(p[["cl_time_max"]])) - 28) < 1
)
```

```{r figure-3}
# Replicates the typical-value curve of Figure 3 of Rathi 2021 (ADC CL
# relative to baseline vs. time). Figure 3 itself shows individual post hoc
# estimates with a LOESS line.
tibble(time = seq(0, 300, by = 1)) |>
  mutate(ratio = exp(p[["cl_time_max"]] * time^exp(p[["lcl_time_hill"]]) /
    (exp(p[["lcl_t50"]])^exp(p[["lcl_time_hill"]]) + time^exp(p[["lcl_time_hill"]])))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "red") +
  geom_line(colour = "darkgreen", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (day)", y = "CL(t) / CL0",
    title = "Typical ADC clearance relative to baseline",
    caption = "Replicates the typical-value trend of Figure 3 of Rathi 2021."
  )
```

# Covariate effects on exposure (Figure 5)

The Results state that a patient with a high baseline sBCMA of 500 ng/mL would
have a 35% lower ADC Ctau than the typical patient. The figure below sweeps each
continuous covariate of the typical patient across its observed range, holding
the others at their typical values, as in Figure 5.

```{r figure-5}
sweep <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble(covariate = "sBCMA (ng/mL)", value = c(2, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000)),
  tibble(covariate = "IgG (g/L)", value = c(1, 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80)),
  tibble(covariate = "Albumin (g/L)", value = c(20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50)),
  tibble(covariate = "Body weight (kg)", value = c(45, 55, 65, 75, 85, 100, 130))
) |>
  mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

sweep_events <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sweep)), function(i) {
  cov <- typ_cov
  col <- c(
    "sBCMA (ng/mL)" = "SBCMA", "IgG (g/L)" = "IGG",
    "Albumin (g/L)" = "ALB", "Body weight (kg)" = "WT"
  )[[sweep$covariate[i]]]
  cov[[col]] <- sweep$value[i]
  make_typical(sweep$id[i], 2.5, cov = cov)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(sweep_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sweep_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, sweep_events,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
)
ref_ctau <- typ |> filter(treatment == "2.5 mg/kg", time == 21) |> pull(Cc)
ref_mmaf <- max(typ$Cc_mcmmaf[typ$treatment == "2.5 mg/kg"])
sweep_res <- sweep_sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(ctau = Cc[time == 21], cmax_mmaf = max(Cc_mcmmaf), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(sweep, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    `ADC Ctau` = 100 * (ctau / ref_ctau - 1),
    `cys-mcMMAF Cmax` = 100 * (cmax_mmaf / ref_mmaf - 1)
  )

sweep_res |>
  pivot_longer(c(`ADC Ctau`, `cys-mcMMAF Cmax`), names_to = "measure", values_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(value, pct, colour = measure)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~covariate, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Baseline covariate value", y = "Change from typical patient (%)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Rathi 2021 (2.5 mg/kg, cycle 1)."
  )

pct_sbcma <- sweep_res |>
  filter(covariate == "sBCMA (ng/mL)") |>
  select(value, `ADC Ctau`)
pct_sbcma |>
  dplyr::rename("Baseline sBCMA (ng/mL)" = value, "ADC Ctau change (%)" = `ADC Ctau`) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Percent change in ADC Ctau from the typical patient (sBCMA 100 ng/mL).")
pct_500 <- pct_sbcma$`ADC Ctau`[pct_sbcma$value == 500]
# The model gives about -29% at 500 ng/mL against the -35% stated in the
# Results (see Assumptions). The gate pins the deterministic model value, which
# depends only on the CL exponent 0.126 and the two-compartment disposition.
stopifnot(abs(pct_500 - (-29.4)) < 1)
```

The model gives a `r round(pct_500)`% change in ADC Ctau at an sBCMA of
500 ng/mL, against the 35% decrease stated in the Results. It gives about +50%
at an sBCMA near 10 ng/mL, which matches the stated +50% for a very low
baseline sBCMA. The sBCMA exponent on CL is printed identically in Table 1 and
the control stream (0.126), so the maintainers record the 500 ng/mL
difference as a deviation between the model and the paper's text, not a
transcription error.

# Virtual DREAMM-2 cohort

Observed data are not public. The virtual cohort draws baseline covariates
from distributions centred on the Table S2 medians and bounded by the
reported ranges: body weight log-normal (median 74 kg), albumin normal (median
39 g/L), sBCMA and IgG log-normal (medians 80 ng/mL and 8.5 g/L, wide spread
to cover the 1.95-2030 ng/mL and 0.3-99.7 g/L ranges), and 46% female. Two arms
of 200 patients receive 2.5 or 3.4 mg/kg as a 30-min infusion every 3 weeks
for three cycles. `OCC` is the cycle number on every record, so each cycle
draws its own cys-mcMMAF inter-occasion deviation.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2021)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2021)
n_arm <- 200
make_cohort <- function(n, dose_mgkg, id_offset) {
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(74), 0.2)), 42.4), 130),
    ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 39, 5), 19), 50),
    SBCMA = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(80), 1.2)), 1.95), 2030),
    IGG = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(8.5), 1.0)), 0.3), 99.7),
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, 0.46),
    STUDY_DREAMM1 = 0L,
    DOSE_LOW = 0L,
    treatment = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg")
  )
  doses <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 21, 42)) |>
    mutate(
      amt = dose_mgkg * WT, rate = amt / (0.5 / 24),
      evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  obs_t <- sort(unique(c(
    outer(c(0, 21, 42), c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 72, 168, 336) / 24, "+"),
    seq(0, 63, by = 1)
  )))
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_t) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(OCC = pmin(floor(time / 21) + 1, 3)) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_arm, 2.5, 0L),
  make_cohort(n_arm, 3.4, n_arm)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events,
  useLinCmt = FALSE, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 7}
# Replicates the layout of Figure 4 of Rathi 2021 (VPC by analyte and dose):
# 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the simulated individual predictions
# (no residual error) over the first three cycles.
vpc <- sim |>
  select(id, time, treatment, ADC = Cc, `Total mAb` = Cc_tab, `cys-mcMMAF` = Cc_mcmmaf) |>
  pivot_longer(c(ADC, `Total mAb`, `cys-mcMMAF`), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(conc > 0) |>
  group_by(analyte, treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), q50 = median(conc), q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, c("ADC", "Total mAb", "cys-mcMMAF"),
    c("ADC (ug/mL)", "Total mAb (nM)", "cys-mcMMAF (nM)")))

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (day)", y = "Concentration",
    caption = "Simulated 5th-95th percentile band and median; layout of Figure 4 of Rathi 2021."
  )
```

```{r cohort-gate}
c1 <- sim |>
  filter(time <= 21) |>
  group_by(id, treatment) |>
  summarise(
    cmax_adc = max(Cc), ctau_adc = Cc[time == 21][1],
    cmax_mmaf_pgml = max(Cc_mcmmaf) * 1045, .groups = "drop"
  )
c1_summary <- c1 |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(across(c(cmax_adc, ctau_adc, cmax_mmaf_pgml), median), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(
  c1_summary |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Dose" = treatment, "Median ADC Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax_adc,
      "Median ADC Ctau (ug/mL)" = ctau_adc, "Median cys-mcMMAF Cmax (pg/mL)" = cmax_mmaf_pgml
    ),
  digits = 2, caption = "Cycle-1 medians of the virtual DREAMM-2 cohort."
)
# Centre-of-distribution gates against the typical patient. The covariate
# draws are centred near the typical patient, so the cohort median sits
# within tens of percent of the typical value; a mis-transcribed CL, volume,
# dose or unit moves it by far more. Over four seeds the 2.5 mg/kg medians
# were 37.7-38.7 ug/mL (ADC Cmax), 1.92-2.22 ug/mL (ADC Ctau) and 699-831
# pg/mL (cys-mcMMAF Cmax, below the typical value because of the large V3 and
# K43 variability), all well inside these bounds.
med <- function(col, trt) c1_summary[[col]][c1_summary$treatment == trt]
stopifnot(
  abs(pct(med("cmax_adc", "2.5 mg/kg"), 36.5)) < 20,
  abs(pct(med("ctau_adc", "2.5 mg/kg"), 2.22)) < 35,
  abs(pct(med("cmax_mmaf_pgml", "2.5 mg/kg"), 917)) < 35
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Product DAR0 back-solved.** The cys-mcMMAF input is the ADC clearance flux
  times an empirical DAR that resets to the drug-product value DAR0 at every
  dose. The control stream reads DAR0 from a dataset column, and no numeric
  value appears in the paper, its supplement or the control streams. The model
  output is linear in DAR0, so the maintainers back-solved it from the
  typical-patient cys-mcMMAF Cavg of 217 pg/mL (Results). That gives
  `mdar = 3.93`, carried as a fixed parameter. Cavg was chosen over Cmax
  because it is an AUC-based measure and less sensitive to the sampling grid.
  Back-solving from the printed Cmax of 917 pg/mL would give 4.30 instead. The
  ratio of the two printed values, 917/217 = 4.23, cannot be reached with the
  printed Table S4 parameters, whose Cmax/Cavg ratio is 3.86 at any DAR0, so no
  single DAR0 matches both. Holding the DAR constant between the paper's
  nominal sampling times, as NONMEM does for `$PK` quantities, gives a ratio
  of 3.71 and does not resolve the difference either. With `mdar = 3.93`, the simulated typical
  cys-mcMMAF Cmax is about 9% below the printed value. Users with a known lot
  DAR can override `mdar` via `ini()`.
- **sBCMA effect at 500 ng/mL.** The Results state that a baseline sBCMA of
  500 ng/mL lowers ADC Ctau by 35%. The model, using the printed CL exponent
  0.126, gives about 29%. The difference is kept, not tuned.
- **Half-life reference.** The printed half-lives of 11.5 and 14.3 days match
  the typical values with V1 = 4.47 L, i.e. without the male V1 factor, while
  the printed typical-patient exposures include it.
- **Unrounded ADC estimates.** Table 1 prints two decimals. The model uses the
  values the authors held constant in the downstream control streams (e.g. CL
  0.936, IMAX -0.327), which round to Table 1.
- **ADC IIV text vs table.** The Results text gives the final CL IIV as
  34.1% CV, and Table 1 prints 35.00%. The table value is used.
- **ADC IIV scale.** Table 1 prints the ADC IIV as percentages without a
  footnote defining them. The maintainers applied the definition that
  Tables S3 and S4 of the same paper footnote, `%CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`,
  so `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`. The Table S4 percentages agree with that
  definition and not with `sqrt(omega^2)` (V3: 0.260 gives 54.5% as
  printed, not 51.0%; K43: 0.956 gives 127%, not 97.8%).
- **IMAX random effect.** IMAX enters as `TVIMAX + ETA` (normal, not
  log-normal). Table 1 reports its variability as 123%, read as
  SD / |theta|, which gives omega^2 = (1.23 x 0.327)^2 = 0.162. This follows the
  convention the same sponsor footnotes in the later Papathanasiou 2025 pooled
  analysis.
- **Residual SIGMA values are variances.** Table 1 (0.019) and Table S3 (0.0516)
  label their residual errors 'additive SIGMA on log scale'. Table S4 lists
  SIGMA1-4. All are treated as NONMEM `$SIGMA` variances, and the model carries
  their square roots as SDs.
- **Unreported covariances set to zero.** The cys-mcMMAF `$OMEGA BLOCK(3)`
  covariance between CL and K43, and the within-occasion IOV covariance between
  CL and V3, are not reported in Table S4 and are set to 0. The resulting
  3 x 3 IIV matrix is positive definite.
- **Occasions.** The control stream builds four IOV slots, for OCC = 1, 2, 3 and
  OCC > 3, with a shared variance (`$OMEGA BLOCK(2) SAME`). The Results attribute
  the IOV to between-cycle differences, so OCC is taken to be the dosing cycle.
- **Naked-antibody elimination.** As in the total-mAb control stream, the
  naked antibody is eliminated at `CL/V1 - Kdec`. For subjects whose
  time-varying ADC elimination rate falls below their Kdec this rate becomes
  negative. That is a property of the published structure and is kept as
  published.
- **Low-dose and study effects.** `DOSE_LOW = 1` reproduces the control-stream
  flag (actual dose not above 1 mg/kg), which covers the DREAMM-1
  dose-escalation levels 0.03-0.96 mg/kg. `STUDY_DREAMM1 = 1` also maps the
  cys-mcMMAF prediction onto the DREAMM-1 VALA assay scale
  (`1.486 x C - 8.360 pg/mL`) and selects the DREAMM-1 residual error. Set
  both to 0 to simulate the DREAMM-2 / PKC-assay setting.
- **Time-varying clearance clock.** The control streams evaluate the CL change
  at the time since the first dose. The model uses rxode2's `t`, so the first
  dose must be at time 0.
- **Naming.** The time-varying CL magnitude is kept on its signed linear scale
  as `cl_time_max` (with an additive `etacl_time_max`), following the existing
  library models with the same additive-eta form. The convention checker's
  log-transform suggestion for it does not apply.
- **Errata.** A Europe PMC search on 2026-10-16 found no correction notice for
  Rathi 2021.
